education.summary: In her 2025 campaign for the State College Area school board, she said the district should prioritize academics over what she called divisive curricula, supported eliminating DEI programs, and called for fiscal responsibility in district spending. She has not published an education platform for the 2026 State House race.
education.short: In 2025 school board run, prioritized academics, supported eliminating DEI programs.

economy.summary: Supports raising the state minimum wage to $15 an hour and adjusting it for inflation over time, saying the current $7.25 wage is not liveable, and supports paid sick time, paid family leave, and overtime pay protections.
economy.short: Supports $15 minimum wage, paid sick time, paid family leave.

taxes.summary: His campaign says he works to reduce taxes and the cost of living for working families and seniors, citing expanded tax credits for seniors and working families and a new state child and dependent care tax credit; he also calls for ending corporate handouts and tax loopholes.
taxes.short: Cites expanded family and senior tax credits; opposes corporate loopholes.

abortion.summary: Says reproductive rights are human rights and pledges to vote to codify Roe v. Wade into Pennsylvania law and to make the state a safe haven for people seeking care from other states.
abortion.short: Pledges to codify Roe v. Wade into Pennsylvania law.

education.summary: Supports fully and fairly funding public education at all levels, citing more than $5.1 million delivered to school districts in his district and $886,000 for safety and mental health services within schools.
education.short: Supports fully funding public education; cites district funding delivered.

healthcare.summary: Supports protecting the expansion of Medicaid, Medicare, and CHIP, lowering the cost of prescription drugs and out-of-pocket expenses, and expanding access to mental health, addiction, dental, and vision services, including telehealth.
healthcare.short: Supports Medicaid, Medicare, CHIP expansion; lowering prescription drug costs.

energy.summary: Supports shifting to a renewable energy economy to address climate change; co-sponsored the Solar for Schools Grant Program and cites $4.4 million in electric vehicle infrastructure funding and $1.7 million for environmental restoration, parks, and trails projects.
energy.short: Supports renewable energy shift; co-sponsored Solar for Schools program.

guns.summary: Supports what he calls common-sense approaches including closing the background check loophole, extreme risk protection order laws, and safe storage of weapons and ammunition in homes with children.
guns.short: Supports closing background check loophole, ERPO laws, safe storage.
